question.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y={x}^{x}\operatorname{tan}⁡x.
$$

First, we find the natural logarithm of both sides and use the product rule for logarithms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{x}\operatorname{tan}⁡x) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{x})+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{tan}⁡x) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =(x)^{′}\operatorname{ln}⁡x+x{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{′}+{[\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)]}^{′} \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x+x\cdot \frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{\operatorname{tan}⁡x}\cdot {sec}^{2}⁡x \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\cdot \frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡x} \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1+\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y(\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1+\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y={x}^{x}\operatorname{tan}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & ={x}^{x}\operatorname{tan}⁡x(\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1+\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x}) \\  & ={x}^{x}(\operatorname{tan}⁡x\operatorname{ln}⁡x+\operatorname{tan}⁡x+\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡x) \\  & ={x}^{x}(\operatorname{tan}⁡x\operatorname{ln}⁡x+\operatorname{tan}⁡x+\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}) \\  & ={x}^{x}(\operatorname{tan}⁡x\operatorname{ln}⁡x+\operatorname{tan}⁡x+\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡x}) \\  & ={x}^{x}(\operatorname{tan}⁡x\operatorname{ln}⁡x+\operatorname{tan}⁡x+{sec}^{2}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$
